items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: it was Nat Cole and Perry Como... I guess that Perry may have had more of a following at the time because of the exposure he got on television.

ctx.x: So I made -- then Nat went out with another show; we took a big show out with Pullman cars -- it was Nat Cole and Perry Como, and Perry was big on television then. And on that show it was Perry Como and Nat Cole, Roy Hamilton, Ralph Marterie band, Peg Leg Bates, Sarah Vaughn, and a cast of thousands, I guess you could say. We only played 5 cities; we played Briggs Stadium in Detroit, we played the stadiums, you know -- Soldier's Field, the Polo Grounds in New York, and the Muni Movie Stadium in Cleveland; you…

superstars, and they both had their followings, but I guess that Perry may have had more of a following at the time because of the exposure he got on television. But I don't think anyone sold any more records than Nat. You know, he was a record seller.

So we did that thing, and then we went to South America in 1960, and that was an experience that I think musicians should have because -- they say music is an international language, and it is -- and that's when you find out that it is. Because our first stop was in Caracas, Venezuela, and from Caracaus we went to Rio. Now, the difference is just amazing, the way the music is. In Caracas, you find they are really heavy in to the rhythms, you know, and the musicians are fair; you know, I'm speaking of the string…
